newsitem.title: USA: Mexicans hand over Texas man on run for 35 years.
newsitem.headline: Mexicans hand over Texas man on run for 35 years.

text.p: A man who escaped from prison 35 years ago was handed over to Texas police on Friday after his capture this week in Mexico.

Ernesto Lopez, 60, had been on the run since November 1962, when he and another inmate sawed through bars at a prison in Richmond, Texas, and fled. He was serving a life sentence for the 1956 rape and killing of 12-year-old Jeannett Mangan in Dallas.

Texas Department of Criminal Justice spokesman Larry Todd said Mexican police captured Lopez, a U.S. citizen, on Thursday in the town of Penjamo in central Mexico. He would not disclose how he had been found, but said police had been watching him for 18 months.
"He gave up without any difficulties," Todd said. Lopez was living with a family and had a job in Mexico, he said. Todd said Lopez had moved around Mexico over the years to avoid arrest.

He said Mexican authorities on Friday took Lopez to the middle of the bridge spanning the Rio Grande at the border city of Laredo, Texas, and gave him to Texas officials. "He's back. He's in custody," Todd said.
Lopez was to be taken to a maximum security prison in Beeville, Texas, where he was to serve out the rest of his sentence.
Todd said Lopez also would face felony escape charges with a maximum punishment of 15 years.
Lopez, then 19, was originally given the death penalty for the 1956 murder, but the sentence was commuted to life in prison by then-Texas Gov. Price Daniel.
Lopez' accomplice in the crime, Simon Rodriguez, was sentenced to 99 years in prison, but served just 14 years before getting out of jail.
